quotes: “ Rachel Lynde ’ s husband ”— was sowing his late turnip seed on the hill field beyond the barn ; and Matthew Cuthbert ought to have been sowing his on the big red brook field away over by Green Gables . Mrs. Rachel knew that he ought because she had heard him tell Peter Morrison the evening before in William J. Blair ’ s store over at Carmody that he meant to sow his turnip seed the next afternoon . Peter had asked him , of course , for Matthew Cuthbert had never been known to volunteer information about anything in his whole life .

“ He doesn ’ t generally go to town this time of year and he never visits ; if he ’ d run out of turnip seed he wouldn ’ t dress up and take the buggy to go for more ; he wasn ’ t driving fast enough to be going for a doctor . Yet something must have happened since last night to start him off . I ’ m clean puzzled , that ’ s what , and I won ’ t know a minute ’ s peace of mind or conscience until I know what has taken Matthew Cuthbert out of Avonlea today .”

“ It ’ s no wonder Matthew and Marilla are both a little odd , living away back here by themselves . Trees aren ’ t much company , though dear knows if they were there ’ d be enough of them . I ’ d ruther look at people . To be sure , they seem contented enough ; but then , I suppose , they ’ re used to it . A body can get used to anything , even to being hanged , as the Irishman said .”
“ This is a real fine evening , isn ’ t it ? Won ’ t you sit down ? How are all your folks ?”
“ I was kind of afraid you weren ’ t , though , when I saw Matthew starting off today . I thought maybe he was going to the doctor ’ s .”
“ Matthew went to Bright River . We ’ re getting a little boy from an orphan asylum in Nova Scotia and he ’ s coming on the train tonight .”
“ Are you in earnest , Marilla ?” she demanded when voice returned to her .

“ Yes , of course ,” said Marilla , as if getting boys from orphan asylums in Nova Scotia were part of the usual spring work on any well-regulated Avonlea farm instead of being an unheard of innovation .
